subject: Deal-focused GPU footprint playbook: per-model KV caching & precision guidance
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Deal-focused GPU footprint playbook: per-model KV caching & precision guidance

Hi Daniel —

Following up from last week's call, attached is the first draft playbook we promised that ties model-specific memory sizing (context / KV cache) and quantization choices to Dedicated capacity commitments. High level notes up front: 

- Goal: map each model variant you want to run in production to a recommended GPU class and reserved pod count, with explicit headroom for KV cache and burst.
- Context targets you mentioned: 8k for standard chat; 32k for specialist retrieval flows; occasional 64k archival reads (cold-path).
- Quantization guidance: fp16 for high-accuracy paths; int8 for most steady-state production; int4 for ultra-cost-sensitive inference where slight quality loss is acceptable.

Key assumptions in the attached: average request rps distribution per variant, KV-cache hit rates (we used 60% prefix reuse for 32k flows), and 20% room for RAG-induced peaks. See novaprospect-memory-table.csv for per-variant memory numbers we used to size pods.

Questions for you so we can finalize:
1) Will you accept int8 for the 32k specialized model?
2) Is the 64k cold-path allowed to be routed to a lower SLA best-effort pool (no reserve)?
3) Any compliance constraints that block offloading or certain quantized runtimes?

Next steps: if you confirm these answers we’ll lock the committed pod counts and provide a canary rollout plan (2-week canary -> scale to committed pool).

Attaching: NP-3742_gpf_playbook_v0.3.pdf (playbook), novaprospect-memory-table.csv (per-variant memory table).

Thanks —
Chloe

Subject: Re: Deal-focused GPU footprint playbook: per-model KV caching & precision guidance

Chloe —

Thanks for the draft. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Cost sensitivity: procurement is pushing for the lowest steady-state cost. That said, product is firm that 32k quality needs to be near current baseline.
- Latency: for the standard 8k chat flows we need p99 < 180ms. For 32k specialized flows p95 < 450ms is acceptable.
- Quantization: product is open to int8 for 32k IF we can validate no >1.5% regression on the evaluation suite. int4 is likely a hard no for 32k.

Can you call out expected p99/p95 latency deltas for switching from fp16 -> int8 for our 13B and 70B variants (both in the table)? Also: what’s the impact on GPU slots if we apply 2:1 packing for int8 workloads?

I looped procurement to get visibility on the committed spend cadence.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: Deal-focused GPU footprint playbook: per-model KV caching & precision guidance

Daniel / Chloe —

Quick numbers from our sizing table (attached as CSV in my reply):

- 13B standard (8k): fp16 baseline = 30 GB GPU memory per replica (including 20% KV headroom); int8 ~= 22 GB (roughly -27%); performance: int8 gives ~1.6x throughput at same latency budget when packed 2:1.
- 13B long (32k w/ KV cached): fp16 baseline = 40 GB (KV cache inflates working set); int8 ~= 30 GB; effective replica throughput for 32k is ~0.6x of 8k baseline due to longer generation and KV lookups.
- 70B standard (8k): fp16 baseline = 110 GB; int8 ~= 78 GB; 70B long (32k) fp16 = 140 GB (KV heavy) — we advise reserved single-GPU 80GB class with dynamic offload for int8, but note int8 offload complexity introduces tail variability.

Packability notes: for int8 steady-state workloads we can safely pack 2 small requests per slot for 13B-class models; for 70B we usually only get mild packing gains (~1.25x) unless you accept higher latency p95.

Latency delta expectations (rough bounds):
- 13B: fp16 -> int8: p99 delta ~ -10 to -25ms (improvement) due to higher throughput and smaller communication overhead when well-packed.
- 70B: fp16 -> int8: p95 delta ~ -30 to -70ms in steady-state packed settings; but p99 tail risk increases if KV offload contention happens.

Implementation caveat: mixing quantized and fp16 variants in the same pool increases scheduling complexity; recommended pattern is separate pools per precision class with autoscale rules and a cross-pool fallback route.

I attached a short CSV with the per-variant numbers I referenced: novaprospect-memory-table.csv

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Deal-focused GPU footprint playbook: per-model KV caching & precision guidance

Looping in ops concerns from the Dedicated side:

- Reserved pool commitments we propose:
  * 13B-int8 pool: 6 replicas (covers 8k & most 32k with prefix reuse assumptions)
  * 13B-fp16 pool: 2 replicas (for exact-quality flows and regen)
  * 70B-int8 hybrid: 3 replicas on 80GB int8-enabled nodes + 1 fp16 fallback node for the heaviest requests

- Burst policy: allow a burst band of +40% for 48 hours (billing-visible) before autoscaling to additional capacity. This gives you headroom during marketing spikes.
- Canary plan: schedule 14-day canary against a 10% traffic slice, validate eval suite quality thresholds and latency SLOs, then convert to committed pool.

Please confirm whether procurement needs a separate line-item for the int8 runtime licensing (we do have a small premium for managed int8 kernels if you want guaranteed tail behavior).

Priyom

Thanks all — summary and next actions: 

1) Daniel: your ask recorded — int8 acceptable for 32k only if eval regression <1.5%. We will run a dedicated eval against your suite during canary.
2) Marcus/Priyom: finalize committed pool counts as proposed above; add explicit cross-pool fallback route in the rollout config.
3) Procurement: please review the optional int8 managed runtime line item; Chloe will share a brief pricing appendix.

I attached NP-3742_gpf_playbook_v0.3.pdf which pulls Marcus's CSV into the final sizing tables and includes a week-by-week canary & handoff checklist. Proposed canary start: 2027-07-11, completion and commit target: 2027-07-25.
